name: weather
author: LLM, from a scenario. NOT hand-tuned numbers — a statement of what good means.
scenario: The Yard's weather (UWeatherSubsystem, CHIMERA_VISION.py) is Law 4's memento mori made mechanical: a storm erases every sand/basin footprint, unconditionally, when it passes. That erasure must happen often enough to ACHE — footprints are not a permanent scrapbook, the world is not a diorama — and rarely enough that prints MATTER: a player who leaves a trail should realistically be able to walk away and come back to find it still there. Gusts should read as living, irregular weather, never a looping mechanical noise. The sky must never sit fully dead-calm, and a storm must never dominate play time — both are absolute rule violations, not matters of taste.

constraints.why: NO PERMANENT STORM — an absolute gate, tested against the WORST of N restarts (not the mean), so one unlucky seed cannot hide a config where storms swallow play. At the seed this sits near 0.003 (35 storms x ~0.5h each against 250 27h-days) — enormous headroom before this bites, which is the point: it exists to catch a genuinely broken mutation (e.g. storm_duration_min drifting toward hours, or storm_period collapsing toward zero), not to shape the winner.

NO DEAD CALM — the other absolute gate, also tested at the WORST restart. dead_calm_fraction is non-storm time that is both night (the calm baseline, IsNight()=40% of every day) AND between gust pulses; it rises if gusts space out far enough that the wind audibly goes silent for long stretches. A world that can sit fully still for more than half of all time is not weather, it is a diorama with a wind cue bolted on.

Storms must arrive on a cadence a player actually experiences across sessions. Below 3 days storms crowd every play session and nothing has time to feel earned; above 14 days a storm becomes a once-in-a-blue-moon event a player may never see happen at all, and the memento mori stops being felt. The seed's own uniform(5,9) -> mean 7.0 sits centered in this band, not pinned against it.

THE LAW-4 TENSION ITSELF, as a ratio so it cannot be gamed by scaling storm cadence alone: mean_footprint_lifetime_days / storm_interval_days_mean. A footprint's lifetime is bounded above by the gap it was born into (nothing can outlive the wipe at the next storm's end), so this ratio is naturally <1 — but it COLLAPSES toward 0 exactly when storms land close enough together, relative to how often the wanderer leaves a print, that a print barely has time to exist before it is gone (the concrete 'too often to matter' failure). The floor demands prints survive a substantial share of their own gap — they were there to be re-found — without requiring the trivial, unfalsifiable case of a ratio pinned at 1.0.

Even the single luckiest footprint, across every restart, must not survive three weeks — a soft companion to the hard storm-time-fraction gate, catching the OPPOSITE failure: storms individually rare enough (not frequent enough) that a print quietly becomes permanent, which breaks the memento mori from the other direction.

No single storm, even the longest ever drawn across every restart, should run for hours — a storm is weather passing through, not a multi-hour lockdown. Secondary and soft: storm_time_fraction is the hard gate against storms DOMINATING time; this catches one individually overlong storm even if the overall time budget still reads fine.

Gusts must read as irregular weather, not a metronome (cv too low — a fixed period is an audibly repeating loop, the exact cliche this system exists to avoid) or pure static (cv too high — gust timing so scattered across orders of magnitude it stops reading as a coherent phenomenon at all). The seed's uniform(8,30) -> cv 0.334 sits centered, not pinned.

Keeps the gust cadence in a perceptible ambient-wind range — loose bounds (a gust every 3 seconds to 2 minutes) that mostly guard against the search finding a degenerate extreme (near-continuous gusting, or gusts so rare they may as well not exist) while leaving the interesting middle wide open.

THE CLIMBING TERM (TRAINING_PROTOCOL.md S3: 'a spec made only of walls gets you exactly the walls' — every constraint above is a wall or a band, and without this the optimiser would stop the moment it cleared them all). A footprint that persists longer is a footprint more likely to be re-found, which is the positive half of Law 4 that mere non-violation cannot express. ref=7.0 sets sat~=0.5 at the seed's own measured lifetime, so there is real room to climb — but only by pushing storms rarer/longer-gapped, which the storm_interval band, the lifetime_period_ratio ceiling, and the longest_footprint_lifetime_days gate all resist. The tension is real: this term wants footprints to last; five other terms above cap how far that can go.
